A hash table is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values. Hash tables use a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found. Collisions occur when two different keys are hashed to the same index. Handling collisions is crucial for the effective functioning of a hash table.
